title_en: Some People Think GTA 6's Jason Showing Any Kind of Affection for Lucia is an Attack on Masculinity Itself – Here's Why That's Dumb
summary_en: Some corners of the internet are furious Rockstar has apparently turned its crime simulator into a game about being a considerate boyfriend, while others are discovering that Jason Duval might just be the perfect man.
body_en:
Of all the things I expected Grand Theft Auto 6 to cause arguments about, whether or not a man should buy his girlfriend flowers was pretty low on the list. Yet some corners of the internet are furious that Rockstar has apparently turned its crime simulator into a game about being a considerate boyfriend, while others are discovering that Jason Duval might just be the perfect man – a sentence I never thought I’d write about a Grand Theft Auto protagonist.
As well as the usual GTA activities of stealing cars, shooting people, and generally being a menace to society, GTA 6 gives players the option to nurture the relationship between its two protagonists, Jason and Lucia. It's especially prevalent at the start of the game, where you can renovate their home, buy Lucia flowers, pick out clothes and accessories for her while shopping, bring her drinks, open car doors, and even hold her hand while walking around Leonida. I think it's all rather sweet, especially when you consider that these two are also quite happy to commit armed robberies together. Couples who crime together, stay together. (That's not a spoiler; that's me high on hopium as I play through the story.)
Crucially, all of this romantic housekeeping is optional. The game certainly prompts you to nurture the relationship, especially early on when we're just finding out who Jason and Lucia are. But when the button-press to hold hands or show affection pops up, you're free to ignore it. Over time, this will cause the relationship to cool to the point where eventually they become platonic partners in crime, but they're still very much in it together.
Showing affection is also not specific to Jason either – once you're through chapter one, which is heavily focussed on the army vet, and deeper into the game where you spend more time as both characters, they can both choose to show the other affection – or not, if you so desire. You choose how much effort they want to put into Jason and Lucia’s relationship, and the game responds accordingly. You can make them the sort of disgustingly loved-up couple who make everyone around them feel slightly ill, or let their relationship cool into something more businesslike. No-one is being forced to play house.
From a quick browse of social media, and, in particular, X, you'll see posts reading "RIP GTA. Killed by women. Like so many before," from @trackthedecline. User @ExoGhost writes, "GTA 6 has a mission where you need to buy flowers for Lucia. This game is such woke slop. It's so obvious it was made by women". And then there's @5jmxgz, who claims, "gta 6 lowk the biggest flop ever, we waited 13 years for a literal cuck simulator."
Grand Theft Auto 6 cemented itself as the most successful entertainment launch of all-time, making $3.79 billion in just one day.
For some players, the problem seems to be that they’ve waited 13 years for a new GTA game, only to find themselves assembling furniture and picking up groceries. There’s a reasonable argument buried somewhere in there about whether mundane domestic activities are what people want from a series built on criminal excess and absolute freedom. If you spend your actual life doing chores, perhaps coming home to do more of them in a video game isn’t particularly appealing? The pace of Chapter 1 feels like deliberate decision from Rockstar to subvert what people expect from GTA, and I think it's that that's causing at least some of the reaction, because once you move onto chapter 2 and beyond, the only chores you're really doing is putting cups in the sink, opening car doors, and getting your significant other a snack now and again. No one is cleaning the oven or pulling lint out of the dryer.
However, some of the complaints go considerably further, treating the idea of Jason showing any kind of affection or consideration for Lucia as an attack on masculinity itself. Some have described the game as a “cuck simulator” while reacting to Jason running errands for Lucia. Apparently buying your girlfriend something nice is now a threat to civilization. Someone should probably warn the florists.
For me, GTA 6 is Rockstar at its subversive best. While internet conflict raged over whether or not games were getting too “woke” and that the heroes were becoming too “soft,” Rockstar gave us a strong, straight, masculine guy with a hot girlfriend. The only catch? You have to put in the work that goes with that. You need to put effort into the relationship to keep the hot girlfriend, you need to go to the gym to stay buff, you need to contribute to the household finances.
Some X users are seeing the positives in Jason and Lucia's dynamic, and the warmth shared between them. "When he said 'you and Tommy are the only family I need', then went ahead to include her mom because he knows how important she is to her. Yep Jason Duval is not just a green flag but the greenest forest," says @keiuzuki. It's a sentiment shared by many others, who are already creating collages, montages, and memes dedicated to Mr Duval.
For plenty of female players, Jason’s appeal isn’t just that he’s attractive, capable, or willing to commit a little light felony in the name of love. It’s that he pays attention. He notices things. He makes an effort. And while the bar for romantic male behavior probably shouldn’t be somewhere around buying flowers and remembering to open a car door, there’s something undeniably appealing about a game that makes those little gestures feel important. The man has a criminal record, questionable career prospects, and presumably several outstanding warrants, but at least he remembers to buy you a lemonade.
There’s also a particularly funny subset of women watching their real-life partners enthusiastically renovate a fictional house, buy fictional flowers, and take their fictional girlfriend shopping, while wondering when exactly that energy might make its way into their actual relationship. Imagine watching your husband spend three hours choosing the perfect paint color for a woman made of polygons while the dishwasher has needed emptying since Tuesday.
Others have even suggested that GTA 6 is having a positive effect on their relationships, with men apparently taking inspiration from Jason’s behavior and becoming more thoughtful partners themselves. Rockstar may have inadvertently created the world’s most expensive couples’ therapy.
"My husband has been playing GTA 6 and took a break to run to the get food", tells Threads user monroecammack. "He came back with ice cream and flowers for me and said 'if I have to get Lucia flowers, then I have to get flowers for you too' and I - ". One reply humurously replied with "OMG THAT IS WHY MY HUSBAND RANDOMLY GOT ME FLOWERS YESTERDAY."
And perhaps that’s the most interesting thing about this whole argument. GTA has always been about giving players the freedom to indulge in fantasies, whether that’s becoming a criminal kingpin, owning an absurd collection of supercars, or escaping the police in increasingly ridiculous ways. GTA 6 simply adds another fantasy to the list: being in a loving, functional relationship, which is truly the most unrealistic thing Rockstar has ever put in one of its games.
To reiterate, Lucia isn’t just sitting around waiting for Jason to bring her presents. She’s a playable protagonist with her own agency, and the relationship mechanics allow both characters to show affection and consideration for one another. This isn’t necessarily about a man serving a woman. It’s about two people making an effort.
Nobody is suggesting that GTA 6 should replace actual relationship advice, and buying your girlfriend flowers isn’t going to magically fix a failing relationship. But there’s something fascinating about watching a game famous for its violence accidentally spark a conversation about emotional labor, affection, and what people expect from their partners. If nothing else, it’s rather telling that in a game where you can steal cars, rob banks, and murder people, one of the most controversial things Jason Duval can do is be nice to his girlfriend. Apparently, Grand Theft Auto is fine. Grand Theft Affection is where some draw the line. Rockstar has made it clear that maintaining their relationship requires effort from both sides. Which makes the outrage over Jason buying flowers even stranger, unless I've missed the part where basic consideration became a gender-specific skill.
Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.
